Why is Gaza drowning? Images of floods engulfing Gaza have gone viral. Most coverage focuses on the humanitarian catastrophe. Few explain what caused it. Since October 2023, Israeli forces have destroyed nearly all of Gaza’s infrastructure. Up to 68 million tons of rubble now blanket the Strip. Homes, schools, hospitals, and basic services have been flattened, with at least 90 percent of the territory destroyed. Now, as winter sets in, the first rains are making what is left unlivable. At least five people have been killed after sand embankments collapsed in the downpour. None of this is new. The Israeli plan to make Gaza unlivable has been unfolding for years. In 2012, the UN warned that Gaza could be unlivable by 2020 because of repeated Israeli assaults, a crippling blockade, the collapse of its aquifer, energy shortages, and mass unemployment. Despite the so-called ceasefire, our reporter in Gaza describes a situation that is impossible to endure: no shelter, no aid, and a ban on rebuilding. Conditions are getting worse by the day.” @specter_affairs

El alto el fuego no ha puesto fin al sufrimiento en Gaza. A los ataques israelíes, que han dejado más de 1.600 palestinos muertos desde su entrada en vigor, se suman ahora las inundaciones que arrasan los refugios de cientos de miles de desplazados. Más de 350.000 personas se han visto afectadas por las inundaciones y unas 70.000 tiendas de campaña han quedado anegadas. Sin acceso suficiente a materiales de emergencia, millones de palestinos siguen expuestos al frío, las aguas residuales y unas condiciones sanitarias cada vez más precarias. La Organización Mundial de la Salud advierte de un aumento de las infecciones respiratorias: se han registrado 33.000 casos más que en el mismo período del año pasado. Palestine is not just a place on a map. Palestine is its people, its history, its culture, its language, its traditions, its children, its mothers, its fathers, and generations of people who deserve to live in peace, freedom, and dignity. You can destroy buildings, but you cannot destroy a people’s identity. You can silence voices, but you cannot erase their stories. You can take away homes, but you cannot take away the memories, the roots, and the love people carry in their hearts. The people of Palestine deserve what every human being deserves: the right to live, the right to feel safe, the right to dream, the right to grow up without fear, and the right to have a future. Behind every headline, every photograph, and every statistic are real human beings. Families. Children. People with dreams, hopes, names, and stories. Their lives matter. Their voices matter. Their suffering must never become something the world simply scrolls past. Supporting Palestine means standing for humanity, justice, freedom, and human dignity. It means refusing to look away. It means remembering those whose voices are not always heard and making sure their stories are not forgotten. To every Palestinian who continues to hold on to their identity, culture, heritage, and hope: the world sees you, the world hears you, and your existence matters. Palestine is not forgotten. Palestine is not invisible. Palestine is not alone. May the children of Palestine know a future filled with peace instead of fear. May families be reunited. May people return to their homes. May justice prevail, and may every human being live with the dignity they deserve. From the river to the sea, may all people live in freedom, safety, and dignity. We will remember. We will speak. We will stand for humanity. FREE PALESTINE 🇵🇸🤍 #palestine #recommendations #fypシ
